name: Orchestrator decides; subagents only gather and verify

name: Typed output schemas with no extra fields
aka: ENDPOINTS CONFIG CONSTANTS MAP RESEARCH REGISTER COMMANDS DUMPFACTS SCAN FINDINGS CITATIONS VERDICT
problem: Free prose from extractors is costly to read and invites unchecked claims; the orchestrator needs results it can read by id and a program can consume.
mechanism: Each agent returns a JSON Schema object. Pure extractors use additionalProperties:false; dependencies are recorded verbatim as declared; mappers cap facts; analysts return FINDINGS with a failing condition; skeptics return a VERDICT.

problem: Both idea sweeps scored ideas against the FixFlow ship plan, never against the 21 bottlenecks, so their verdicts could not be carried over.

problem: FixFlow's written warnings (empty eas.json env value, Sentry plugin in app.json, hmac.compare_digest, railway up from root) rely on being read. A lint or deny rule makes each trap mechanical.

problem: FixFlow's CLAUDE.md and 24k characters of skill and agent descriptions may load more than needed or contradict each other, costing context and obedience.

problem: Choosing a model tier and effort level for reviewers and verifiers is guesswork. We need fair, pre-scored trials and a usage sensor before changing effort or stop rules.

problem: FixFlow's phase routine can skip steps or trust the wrong document. Small written rules fix precedence, the opening of a phase, journal entries, stop rules and mockups.

problem: Saved workflow scripts, briefs and skills can pile up without evidence they are used, and later replays cannot tell which version was run.

problem: Native web and mobile test runs print long output into the session. A wrapper that prints one result line plus counts could save tokens.

name: Secrets and private-data handling in briefs
problem: Sessions holding production credentials could leak secrets or read injected text. Briefs and agent types should keep secrets out of reach.
mechanism: Pass secrets by variable name only; committed records name the variable not the value; agents never read .env; a restricted research agent type with deny rules and no web tools in sessions holding prod credentials.

name: Workflow-script hygiene borrows from BAML
problem: Gate scripts can mislabel a failure as a usage limit, give a skeptic contaminating inputs, trust an agent's own list of reads, or use a field name that triggers a billed refusal.
mechanism: Tagged run() results separating null, error and value; a pure skeptic-input function; compare an agent's self-listed reads with its transcript; avoid naming a verdict field 'reasoning', rename to 'explanation'.

name: Planner: lanes a little below the knee
problem: Parallel sessions were chosen by feel; past the lowest limit extra lanes add only queues, tokens and collisions, no speed.
mechanism: Before work starts, compute how many lanes the four limits (check, review, merge, token window) and memory allow: one lane delivers 1 ÷ (cycle time); knee = lowest limit ÷ that. Run about 0.8 × knee.
origin: Coined in the harness v2 design (docs/program/HARNESS-V2-DESIGN-2026-11.md); loop B5
status_note: Plan accepted 11 Nov; nothing installed or wired. Shown only in the model and demos.
results: Not yet tested live. In the model, a lane past the knee only waits, so the planner gives nearly the same finish on fewer lane-hours [I]. Testbed: about three lanes worth running, build ran six to nine [M].
potential: Fewer sessions open for the same finish: fewer tokens and less memory [I]. Ten lanes at once lasted about 15 minutes [M], so right-sizing could avoid the limit stop.
next_step: Measure the rates (check time, review time) in phases 2-3; the planner then recomputes the chart per plan.
owner_decision: None specific; part of plan acceptance (D01, answered yes to phase 1).

name: Plan check: footprints, two graphs, refuse collisions
aka: Parallel work is planned, not discovered
problem: Slices ran in parallel with nothing checking for collisions; the first check on merged main failed for the first two slices because of hand edits to shared documents.
mechanism: Every slice declares files written, interfaces read, prerequisites, shared things (migration number, port, database), risk and size. Build a needs-graph and a collides-graph, refuse plans with two writers of one file, refuse branches that touch outside their footprint, and feed real touches back.
origin: Coined in the harness v2 design; orchestration document had no dependency graph or footprint check
status_note: Spec complete (8 steps). The testbed never laid slices out with footprints, so there is no real plan to replay; sample plan is made up.
results: Not yet tested. The testbed's first-check failures on merged main for the first two slices were hand-edit collisions [M].
potential: Shortest finish set by the longest weighted chain of needs; a re-split pays only if it shortens that chain or fills an idle lane.
next_step: Write the plan-check section into the orchestration document when the owner says so; touch-list test on ten recorded cases.
owner_decision: Whether to add the section to the orchestration document (it belongs to the ship plan's pull request).

name: Scheduler: two at a time, waits parked outside sessions
problem: After a stop every session was released at once and waited together, holding context and burning tokens; one check then waited 2,030 s.
mechanism: Turn the wave plan into running sessions, release at most two at a time (one new slice per five minutes in the model), keep waiting slices parked outside any session, and bring sessions back after a stop.

results: Not yet tested. Record: two at a time got further, 18 of 48 agents finished in one window [M]; a lean run finished 30 of 31 [M].

name: Governor: slow lanes so the token window lasts
problem: At the five-hour window's limit every lane stops at once; 14 limit episodes in October.
mechanism: Keep governor share = what the window can still carry ÷ what lanes would burn, using measured tokens per lane-hour by model, so lanes slow instead of everything stopping.

results: Not yet tested. Record: one window covered about 3.4 million subagent tokens [M]; subagents caused 91 of 104 limit errors [M].

name: Gate workflow: review runs outside the root
problem: The root briefed reviewers, read the last diff, ran the check twice and edited the board by hand; nothing could leave faster than the root.
mechanism: Reviewers run in a saved workflow, one gate at a time, write reports to disk and return a typed verdict naming the commit they read. Tested first with stand-in agents; first a probe that a workflow agent can run the check at all.

problem: High-risk merges went in without anyone reading the final commit (5 of 6); the root merged and edited the board by hand.
mechanism: A local script merges one at a time under a lock with one check on the merged result, records who read the final head, and refuses high-risk branches on 'nobody' or 'its own session'. Record-only first, refusal after the owner decides.

name: The library: harness memory that updates itself
problem: Sessions re-read the same files and re-solve problems; the planner and governor have only guessed rates. No library or index was ever tried in the testbed.
mechanism: Six SQLite tables rebuilt from a git journal (journal, entry/handle/footprint_item, state, edge, rate, lookup). Written by tools at the moment of truth, asked never pushed, every lookup counted.
origin: Coined in design; builds on the knowledge-store design (PR #183)

problem: Libraries fill with things no longer true; the board carried 183 minor findings with no status.

aka: Entry retires into a lint, test or gate clause

problem: A lookup library that fails silently never improves, and nobody knows when it should have answered.
mechanism: When a session solves what the library already held, record the miss and its cause and fix the lookup keys. The lookup table counts hit or miss, tokens returned.

problem: Which limit comes first depends on guessed times and an unknown token window; plans are laid out on guesses.

problem: Files repeat in reading (65-76% [E] of reading) while questions do not, so re-reading files is the repeating cost.

name: Pathway map: graph of states, trees as views
problem: One walked pathway is not a diversity; the owner wanted the library's pathways mapped and measured before any fix.
mechanism: A declarative graph of 40 [M] states and 83 [M] branches across eleven stages. Three ways of working run on the same pieces of work: strong model directly, cheap ladder, and cheap with library. Trees show every route.
origin: The owner proposed trees, ensemble models and graphs, 2026-11-12; built by the orchestrator in docs/program/library-pathways/.

name: Ensemble of runs with rank-correlation ranking
problem: Most rates are unknown guesses, so a single answer would mislead; the owner wants the spread and which unknowns matter most.
mechanism: 1000 runs per tie draw each unknown across its range, with shared levels per group, and report percentiles plus Spearman rank correlation of each unknown with each ratio.
origin: The owner's 'ensemble models' suggestion, 2026-11-12; built in the pathway map.
status_note: The spread follows from the ranges and the draw, not a measurement of the library.
results: Cost against the ladder at tie 0: 1.04 [G] (1.01 to 1.10); runs cheaper with a wrong rate no higher: 0.3% [G] at tie 0 and 6.1% [G] at tie 1.

name: Funnel of a hundred pieces of work
problem: Show where library benefit is lost between a task arriving and the cheap model producing a right answer.
mechanism: Start with 100 pieces of work the cheap model would get wrong alone; count how many survive each stage: entry held, looked up, right entry comes back, good entry, passes screen, in the window, cheap attempt right.
status_note: Bars match to design steps by hand.
results: Middle values: 13.1, 4.8, 2.3, 1.3, 1.1, 0.97, 0.35 [G]; all-good setting ends at 31.7 [G].
potential: All-good end 31.7 [G] of 100 pieces.

name: Three conditions and eight corners
problem: Find which conditions must hold for the library to beat the ladder.
mechanism: Group library unknowns into comes back, reach, entry quality (plus running cost); set each at its poor or good end across eight corners and an 11-by-11 reach-by-quality square.
origin: Orchestrator's revision 4, 2026-11-12, after the check of the second build.
status_note: Group placement is a judgment; corners move up to 0.2 under other placements.
results: Only all three good beats the ladder: cost 0.82 [G], wrong 0.67 [G]. High reach with poor entries: cost 1.43 to 1.53 [G], wrong 1.56 to 1.71 [G]; low reach corners about 1.0 [G].
potential: All-good: 0.75 [G] cost and 0.67 [G] wrong rate over the ladder.
cite: docs/program/LIBRARY-PATHWAYS-2026-11.md:50 — "Much comes back, high reach, good entries | 0.82 | 0.67"

name: Two weights per limitation: alone and last
problem: A fix tested alone measures as nothing because steps multiply; the real size of a limitation shows when it is the last one left.
mechanism: Alone moves only its unknowns to their good ends; last leaves only it at middle values while all else is good. Both are shares of the full fall (30.6% [G]).
status_note: Weights are shares of a guessed fall; they do not add up.
results: Entry quality alone 6.0%, last 104.1% [G]; step 4 alone 10.9%, last 94.0% [G]; no single measured limitation left alone puts the library above the ladder.
cite: docs/program/LIBRARY-PATHWAYS-2026-11.md:77 — "Alone: what moving only this gives. ... Last: what is lost if only this stays."

name: Knowledge store of solved problems (memoization with invalidation)
problem: The same hard defect or build trap gets re-solved at an expensive model tier each time it recurs, because past diagnoses live only in prose nobody can query by symptom.
mechanism: After a hard problem is solved, the solver records symptom, cause, failed attempts, fix, what the fix depends on, and a check proving the cause is present. Later a cheap agent looks it up, runs the check, and reuses the fix.
origin: The owner's need of 2026-11-02, in docs/program/KNOWLEDGE-STORE-DESIGN-2026-11.md (v1.3.1, PR #183); framing from caching and case-based-reasoning literature.
status_note: Research and design complete at v1.3.1; nothing built. Owner's next step is D1, the free recurrence audit, then a second yes (D1b).
results: Not yet tested. Pilot has a kill criterion. Recurrence base rate: 3 to 5 same-cause repeats among 48 fix commits on main (M, counted).
potential: Cheap agent reuses a fix instead of a Fable/Opus re-derivation; early value in build/deploy traps checkable without Docker. No saving figure stated.
next_step: Run D1: one Sonnet audit session plus an Opus refuter pass over the 48 fix commits; stop and ask the owner.
owner_decision: D1 (run the audit), then D1b (go on to build) after seeing the audit number.

name: Journal of immutable event files plus rebuildable SQLite index
problem: Several sessions, worktrees and hosts must read and write one store safely, with full history and no lost writes, on a Windows box with no database server.
mechanism: Truth is an append-only journal: one canonical-JSON file per event, named by its sha256, in a private git repo outside all worktrees. A per-host SQLite file is a rebuildable projection of it, with a watermark.
origin: Event-sourcing and provenance lanes T-02, E-09 (Fossil, git-bug, Beads); this design's lane rulings KS-R1.
status_note: Specified in section 3.1 and the write path; build phases KS-1 onward, none started.
results: Not yet tested as a system. Write-path numbers measured on this box: rename-over-existing failed 99-126 times per 8x1,000 identical events (M); freshness check 23-35 ms at 5,000 events (M).
potential: Pure-add merges need no merge driver; a broken index is deleted and rebuilt, never migrated.
next_step: Build in KS-1 core phase after the audit and owner go.
owner_decision: None before the pilot; store home path and VPS are set up later.
cite: docs/program/KNOWLEDGE-STORE-DESIGN-2026-11.md:224 — append-only, immutable event records: one canonical-JSON file per event (keys sorted, integers only, UTF-8, LF), named by the sha256

name: Entry with diagnosis path, negative results and do-not-apply kind
problem: The costly part to save is what failed and why, which a cheap agent cannot rebuild and a strong agent is likely to retry. Some prescribed fixes are wrong and must be flagged.
mechanism: Each entry has an immutable identity plus an event stream: symptom-first title, cause, manifestation conditions, ordered diagnosis steps, fix, scoped failed approaches with proof level, validity predicate. Kinds include do_not_apply and open_defect. Corrections are new versions.
origin: KEDB/ITIL, case-based reasoning (Aamodt and Plaza), ReasoningBank; worked example ex6 (login lock must keep blocking a correct PIN).
status_note: Schema in section 3.2; fix text withheld until an applies gate run exists, except do-not-apply prohibitions.
results: Not yet tested. Eight worked examples reconstructed from git history show which are lead-capable today.
potential: Stops the repeat of a refuted fix (ex6, ex3); reduces repeat dead ends.
next_step: Seed the eight worked examples as the first entries (seed phase).
owner_decision: Owner confirms only do-not-apply entries that encode an owner decision.
cite: docs/program/KNOWLEDGE-STORE-DESIGN-2026-11.md:243 — approach, why_failed (one or two sentences, distilled), failure_class

name: Eight handle kinds with canonicalised error templates
problem: The same root cause shows up with different error text, in different files and words, so one key per entry would miss or mis-merge symptoms.
mechanism: Each entry carries several key types: canonical error template, tool+phase signature, top in-app frames, command context, prose paraphrases, author-named identifiers, doc pointers, action intents. A mask pipeline scrubs ids and numbers; each key keeps its recipe version and raw text.
origin: Sentry, Drain, Socorro, Windows Error Reporting crash-signature practice (lane T-04); write-time paraphrase from doc2query.
status_note: Section 3.3; recipe is code with golden fixtures built from the repo's own traps.
results: Not yet tested. Selectivity check example: ex6's diff yields 113 tokens firing on 91% of commits (M), so handles are author-named, not derived.
next_step: Build canonicaliser with golden fixtures in KS-2.
cite: docs/program/KNOWLEDGE-STORE-DESIGN-2026-11.md:253 — Eight handle kinds, each with a stated failure mode

name: Retrieval pipeline with score-free abstention (miss / candidate / lead)
problem: At a few hundred entries, a wrong hit acted on is the dangerous failure; a miss is cheap. Raw search scores cannot serve as confidence.
mechanism: Canonicalise and scrub, exact-handle prefilter, three-table BM25 ranking, then abstain on score-free features (exact hit, IDF-weighted coverage, margin). Output is miss, candidate or lead, max one of each, inside a 2,000-character cap.
origin: Lane T-03 (BM25 at tiny scale, BEIR); coverage and margin features coined in this design.
status_note: Section 4.1-4.2; thresholds proposed in KS-2, frozen in KS-4.
results: Not yet tested. Starting values theta_lead 0.5, theta_cand 0.3, margin 0.2 (S, owner parameters).
next_step: Prototype on a synthetic corpus in KS-2, calibrate on seeded entries in KS-4.
cite: docs/program/KNOWLEDGE-STORE-DESIGN-2026-11.md:303 — A BM25 value only orders results within one query; it is never a threshold or a confidence

name: Gate: checks with control pairs, run in isolation
problem: A hit must not be applied just because it looks similar; agents copy near-matching records, wrong ones included. Text checks can pass vacuously.
mechanism: Each lead-capable entry stores a declarative check plus a control pair: it must read PRESENT on a known-broken commit and ABSENT on a fixed one, or it is refused. Runner reads its own artifact, returns applies / not_applies / inconclusive, runs in Docker.
origin: Lanes X-02, M-03 (Getafix, SapFix), M-02 (Ghosh et al.); red-team defects RT-01..09 from the owner's clinic project.
status_note: Declarative half in KS-3 (no Docker); executable half in KS-6b (Docker). Section 3.4.
results: Not yet tested. Two naive probes inverted in an earlier proposal and are kept as golden negative fixtures.
potential: Zero acted-on false leads is the target (T).
next_step: Build the declarative probes over parsed data first (eas.json, app.json, lockfiles).
owner_decision: Enabling scripted checks needs owner approval; Docker start for the two gate phases.
cite: docs/program/KNOWLEDGE-STORE-DESIGN-2026-11.md:276 — A check whose controls do not flip is refused at write time

name: Footprints and traces; invalidation by events, never by time
problem: A stored fix goes stale when the code, version or platform it depends on changes. Age is a poor stand-in for that.
mechanism: Each entry lists typed dependencies (file blob hashes, config keys, versions, env probes). A changed item marks the entry suspect for that caller; the gate re-runs. If controls still flip, the trace is re-stamped (early cutoff) and the entry stays useful.
origin: Build Systems a la Carte, Shake, Bazel, rustc red-green (lane T-01); no prior art found that invalidates by code dependency.
status_note: Section 3.5 and 5; symbol-level spans wait for KS-6b, whole-file hashes until then.
results: Not yet tested.
potential: Fills a gap in prior art; avoids mass invalidation.
next_step: Implement file_blob and config_key items in KS-3.
cite: docs/program/KNOWLEDGE-STORE-DESIGN-2026-11.md:340 — No TTL, no review dates, no scheduled sweep

name: Diff-time warnings for do-not-apply and open-defect entries
problem: A forbidden change (a refuted fix, an open defect) never raises an error, so error-triggered lookup cannot stop it before it merges.
mechanism: At first commit, PR-ready, in the Opus review and inside ks close, the CLI matches identifiers on changed lines against author-named handles and protected files, printing one warning line per matched entry. The reviewer quotes the lookup line and answers each warning.
origin: The owner's critique of v1.2 (section 12.7, KS-O10), narrowed by refuter pass KS-P1..P27.
status_note: Declarative part in KS-3; becomes a go criterion at the pilot (D8). Section 7.2 and 7.6.
results: Not yet tested; offline replay against git history is planned. Measured on history: ex4's handles would have warned on 13 of 154 past commits (M), against 47 for a file-level join (M).
next_step: Build the diff join in KS-3; replay history in the pilot.
owner_decision: False-alarm ceiling (one warning per ten unrelated past commits) is an owner parameter.

name: Step-zero lookup before escalating a tier
problem: Escalating to Opus or Fable without checking whether the problem was already solved pays the top tier for a repeat.
mechanism: Before escalating, retrying a failed build, or applying a prose-prescribed fix, the session runs ks lookup on the captured error file. On a lead a cheap agent verifies; on a miss it claims and escalates with only the lookup id in the brief.

results: Not yet tested. Compliance is self-reported; no hook exists.

name: Write-through at solve time, confirmed by the PR's Opus reviewer
problem: Entries written later from a transcript lose the diagnosis path or fill the store with junk; a self-confirmed entry could be wrong.
mechanism: The solving session fills a fixed schema with ks record before PR-ready, only for problems that needed escalation, two failed tries or a burned build. The PR's Opus reviewer tries to refute it and approves it. Cheap agents only append mechanical events.

name: Missed-existing check at record time with blind re-rule
problem: A pull-only store cannot see lookups that missed an entry that existed, so its recall is unknown and the embedding decision has no evidence.
mechanism: When recording, the author names preceding lookups; the CLI lists roster entries that might match and the author rules same/related/new. The reviewer re-rules blind. Reviewer-agreed vocabulary-class same rulings count toward the embedding trigger.

problem: Two parallel sessions can both miss on the same symptom and pay twice to solve it.
mechanism: The first ks claim wins a sequence number inside one write transaction; the second sees who is solving it and may wait, try another hypothesis, or pick other work. Nothing blocks. The solver's record carries the sequence as a fencing token.

problem: With a pull-only store, 'useless' and 'never consulted' look identical from outside.
mechanism: The closing message reports escalations made without a lookup (self-reported, cross-checked against dispatch records). ks close reports whether a diff lookup exists at the PR's final head; reviewers record missed_dna for forbidden changes that merged unwarned.

name: SQLite via node:sqlite as the single engine
aka: one engine one form one CLI
problem: Choose a store engine that needs no install, no daemon, no telemetry, and runs on a Windows dev box and a Linux VPS for a few hundred rows.
mechanism: Use SQLite built into Node 24 (FTS5 for BM25 and trigram, JSON, WAL), one file per host, outside all worktrees, SQLite 3.51.3 or later. Postgres, DuckDB, better-sqlite3, Meilisearch, sqlite-vec stay in reserve behind an abstraction layer.
origin: Eleven engine lanes E-01..E-11 plus X-01; verified in the main session on 2026-11-02.
status_note: A bounded engine trial was rejected: no two candidates were close.
results: WAL multi-process test: 4 writer processes, 12,000 rows, integrity ok (M). Graph-style lineage queries 0.07-95 ms (M).
next_step: KS-1 core uses node:sqlite.
cite: docs/program/KNOWLEDGE-STORE-DESIGN-2026-11.md:402 — Query engine: SQLite through `node:sqlite`

name: Rejected engines, memory products and graph databases
aka: Cassandra, Neo4j, vector servers, hosted memory
problem: The owner asked that no decades-old problem be re-invented and that no database be faked with Markdown; broad discovery had to rule alternatives in or out.
mechanism: Each candidate was scored against local-only data, Windows, telemetry-off and one-developer cost. Cassandra, ClickHouse, Neo4j, Qdrant, hosted agent-memory products and others were rejected or kept as design references only.

status_note: Most are rejected as components; Postgres, DuckDB and Dolt are reserve swap targets.
results: Verdicts only; e.g. Cassandra needs an 8 GB RAM floor and has a 5-7 orders-of-magnitude scale gap (S, vendor docs).
next_step: None; revisit only if a logged trigger fires.

problem: Pure keyword search misses paraphrases with no shared words. It is unknown whether vectors would help at this size.
mechanism: None in v1. If reviewer-agreed vocabulary-class misses reach k >= 3 over n >= 10 examined lookups, add sqlite-vec and a pinned local small embedder inside the same file. A dense-only hit may reach candidate, never lead.

status_note: Trigger not yet measurable; no evidence either way at this scale.
results: Not yet tested.

name: Store home off-machine: private git repo to the owner's VPS over SSH
problem: The store must survive a PC loss and a restart without leaking code or defect data to a third party, and must not be hidden by Windows app virtualisation.
mechanism: Journal lives in a private repo at the profile root, outside worktrees, OneDrive, AppData and bind mounts; pushed to a bare repo on the owner's VPS; a code allow-list refuses github.com. ks doctor checks the path and SQLite version.
origin: Lanes T-06, X-01, E-09; KS-F1 finding on MSIX AppData virtualisation.
status_note: VPS push available from phase P3b; first-stage plan is a one-way backup.
results: Not yet tested. Backup under 4 writers: integrity ok, restore then write ok (M).
next_step: ks init and ks doctor in KS-1; SSH setup once the VPS exists.

name: Scrub before write and on return
problem: Entries could store secrets, phone numbers or customer data, and everything an agent reads reaches Anthropic.
mechanism: Local scrubber: exact redaction of live secrets, token and connection-string regexes, Pakistani phone and CNIC patterns, typed placeholders; fails closed on write. Names and addresses cannot be detected, so raw production output is never stored.
origin: Lane X-06; secretlint and gitleaks as references.
status_note: gitleaks second pass is an owner decision (D5).
results: Not yet tested; a known-miss fixture shows the name/address limit in every test run.
next_step: Build in KS-1 with must-survive fixtures.
owner_decision: D5 (gitleaks); rule on the scope of data reaching Anthropic.
cite: docs/program/KNOWLEDGE-STORE-DESIGN-2026-11.md:354 — fail closed on write, reporting the finding type never the value

name: Pull-only lookup with a hard output cap, no always-loaded lessons
problem: Putting every lesson in CLAUDE.md taxes every agent's context on every call, whether or not the lesson applies.
mechanism: Nothing is pushed into context. One lookup prints at most one lead and one candidate within 2,000 characters; a miss is one line; the error is read from a file so it is not re-emitted. Plan to move diagnostic detail out of CLAUDE.md after a pilot pass.
origin: Harness review rulings; Gloaguen et al. study of repository context files.
status_note: Cap about 860 tokens at 0.4 tokens/char (M).
results: Not yet tested.
potential: CLAUDE.md fixed overhead is about 7.5k tokens per agent (E) that could shrink.
next_step: Implement cap in KS-2.
owner_decision: Moving CLAUDE.md stories out waits on the pilot.
cite: docs/program/KNOWLEDGE-STORE-DESIGN-2026-11.md:35 — The store is pull-only: nothing is ever pushed into an agent's context.

name: ks CLI plus a project skill as the agent interface
problem: Subagents and workflow agents need one access path that works with no configuration or approval prompt.
mechanism: A zero-dependency Node CLI called through Bash: lookup, verify, show, outcome, claim, record, close. A skill (description 300-400 characters) carries the procedure; an MCP wrapper over read verbs is optional and later.
status_note: No hook in v1. D15 (MCP wrapper) and D21 (edit-time hook, default off) held.
results: Not yet tested. Skill description at its ceiling would add about 620 tokens per call (E).
next_step: Build CLI in KS-2; skill after.
cite: docs/program/KNOWLEDGE-STORE-DESIGN-2026-11.md:440 — There is no hook in v1: the store is pull-only and injects nothing.

name: ks close at phase end: anchor, rescan, four counts
problem: Fixes can be pushed after their PR merged and stay stranded off main; entries drift after refactors.
mechanism: One command re-points controls to the squash commit by patch-id, reads blobs at origin/main, re-runs declarative probes, labels results 'fix not on main' or 'regression', re-runs diff lookup over the merged commit, and syncs. Prints four counts.
origin: Real shape of ex8 (a fix stranded for 16 days); KS-F13.
status_note: Section 5.2.
results: Not yet tested.
next_step: Build in KS-3/KS-5.

name: Feedback loop that revises entries (not time decay)
problem: Entries should improve with use without an LLM rewriting them or confirming wrong hits.
mechanism: applies then resolved gives a confirm and may propose a new handle. applies then not_resolved refutes the entry at that footprint and queues an Opus revision. Proposals activate only on a different Opus approver or two independent confirmations.
origin: Case-based reasoning (retrieve, reuse, revise, retain); ACE counters; design KS-R2/R3.
status_note: Section 4.3; working-tree not_when needs Opus approval.
results: Not yet tested.
next_step: Build with record path.

name: Design adjudicated by research sweep, judge panel and refuters
problem: A design from one session carries unchecked claims; the owner wanted broad research before any build.
mechanism: Four workflows: a 57-agent research sweep, a 7-agent judge panel, 31 refuters plus a completeness critic, then the owner's critique and a 7-agent refuter pass over its three new mechanisms. Raw outputs kept with a sha256 manifest.
origin: docs/ORCHESTRATION-DESIGN-2026-10.md method: main session judges, Sonnet researches, Opus proposes and refutes.
status_note: Applied to this design; narrowed all three owner-critique mechanisms, changed no component.
results: About 15M subagent tokens (M) across first three workflows; 30 refuter verdicts plus owner critique KS-O1..O20 and KS-P1..P27 folded in.
next_step: Reuse the pattern for other designs.

name: Automatic footprint capture from hooks, coverage or transcript
problem: Authors may forget to list what an entry depends on; the list should be captured, not guessed.
mechanism: Three captures: hook or transcript logs (what the agent read), coverage of the discriminating check (what it executed), and a fixed environment probe. Over-capture costs a recheck; under-capture risks a false hit.
status_note: Pilot uses fix diff, check inputs, environment probes and transcript reads only; coverage deferred (D5); needs two small dev-dependency additions.

mechanism: About 260 words added to the ship plan section 0 after the pilot says go: lookup before escalation, diff lookups at first commit and PR-ready, ks record before PR-ready, ks close at phase end; reviewer quotes the diff lookup's first line.

name: Seed the store per entry through the write gate
problem: A new knowledge store starts empty, and bulk-copying old prose into it would import errors, contradictions and untested claims.
mechanism: Seed only the eight worked examples plus four CLAUDE.md traps, each through ks record, capture and control, approved by a different Opus session. After that, seed lazily: an entry is written only when a lookup misses and the solving session finds the answer in old prose.
origin: Knowledge-store design (PR #183), ruling KS-R9; grafts from proposals C and D
status_note: Phase KS-4 builds it; blocked until KS-1 to KS-3 exist and the owner says yes to D1b.
results: not yet tested. Seed inventory counted: about 20 solved entries, 21 traps, some 60 negative results (M); about 128 open defects stay in the register.

name: Negative results stored with their validity footprint
problem: A note that says 'approach X failed' goes stale silently, for example after an SDK upgrade, and later blocks a fix that would now work.
mechanism: A refuted claim or ruled-out alternative enters the store only with the footprint it was observed on (for example expo-location 18.0.10). It is a lead scoped to that footprint and is re-verified when the footprint changes. No footprint, no entry.
origin: Knowledge-store design; ruling KS-R2 (research lane T-01 over T-02)
status_note: Part of the seed rules and the fold; not built.
results: not yet tested.
potential: Keeps roughly 60 seed negative results usable without becoming folklore.

problem: Docs disagree with each other and with git (HANDOFF A2 prescribes what CLAUDE.md forbids; migration 0045 both free and merged), so any store seeded from them would store errors.
mechanism: KS-4 resolves each contradiction against git and opens one docs PR with the corrections, each linking its entry id. The PR ships even if the knowledge-store track stops.

results: not yet tested. Seven named contradictions listed (M).

name: Recurring defect shapes as reviewer checklist
problem: The seven recurring defect shapes (for example 'tests pinned the broken behaviour') have no symptom to look up and no fix, so they cannot be store entries.
mechanism: They become a seven-line checklist block in the Opus reviewer's refute brief, beside the register ids the reviewer must try to break. A shape becomes an entry only when a concrete case with a check occurs.

name: Retrieval thresholds frozen with the seed
problem: If the pilot can tune its own thresholds it grades itself, and no literature supplies thresholds for this kind of store.
mechanism: KS-4 ends with a leave-one-handle-out replay over the seeded entries and freezes the lead threshold 0.5, candidate threshold 0.3 and margin 0.2 as config events. The pilot may not change them.
status_note: Values are inferred owner parameters, not design facts.
results: not yet tested. Small samples bound only coarsely: 0 failures in 40 means 7.5 percent or less (S).

name: Net-zero CLAUDE.md edit, then trim to rules plus ids
problem: CLAUDE.md is loaded by every agent every session and must stay honest, yet the store adds a runtime that CLAUDE.md's own rule says to document.
mechanism: KS-1 rewrites the CI row in place (no new line). After the pilot, KS-7 keeps each invariant's rule sentence plus a store id, moves diagnostic paragraphs into verified entries, shrinks the four build traps to one line each; MEMORY.md gains one pointer line.

name: Pull-only lookup with no hook, per clinic lessons
problem: Machinery that pushes extra context into every turn showed no measurable gain in the clinic testbed and costs tokens on every call.
mechanism: Agents run ks lookup on demand; nothing is pushed or hooked. Start with a free audit and an explicit owner yes, a pilot with a kill criterion, and a stop point before any Docker, sync or wiring.
origin: Clinic testbed research (C-01 F18, F19, F21; X-05 F12; M-02 32)
status_note: Evidence for no-hook is about always-loaded files and a rejected error-injection hook, not a lookup hook; a hook is D21, default off.
results: Clinic synthetic trials showed identical acceptance with and without a context projection (M, per source).
potential: Near-zero cost in quiet phases.

name: Recurrence audit before any build
problem: It is unproven that the same cause ever hits twice in ways a symptom-keyed store could serve, so a build could repay nothing.
mechanism: One Sonnet session classifies all fix commits over every ref (72 fix commits, de-duplicated by patch-id), counting a repeat only if a symptom existed, git grep and CLAUDE.md could not find it, and diagnosis was non-trivial. An Opus refuter rechecks ten rows and every counted repeat.
status_note: No code, no install; ready whenever the owner says D1 yes.
results: not yet run. Raw count already 3 to 5 same-cause repeats among 48 fix commits on main (M).
potential: Gives the recurrence prior that decides whether to build.
next_step: Owner answers D1; Sonnet extracts, Opus refutes.
owner_decision: D1 run the audit (default yes); D1b build after reading it (default no).

name: Journal-first store: event files plus SQLite index
problem: Lessons must be shared across worktrees and hosts, survive merges, and be rebuilt after a loss without grepping markdown files.
mechanism: Immutable content-hashed event files in a git store are authoritative; a disposable SQLite index per tool version serves lookups. No-replace publisher (linkSync), freshness check, deterministic fold, commit lease, backup and restore, tested with 8+ processes and 1,000+ writes.
origin: Proposal D (judge-panel graft) on proposal A; refuter fixes KS-F1..F6
status_note: Phase KS-1, Opus implements; waits for D1b yes and idle Opus.
results: not yet built. Refuters measured about 18,300 writes from about 1,500 processes with no corruption (M).
potential: A rebuildable shared memory with no always-on service.
next_step: KS-1 after D1b.
owner_decision: D3 store home; D4 narrow ownership; D6 separate Node 24 CI workflow.

name: Canonicaliser, scrubber and abstaining retrieval
problem: A repair-time lookup must return the right earlier diagnosis, never a plausible wrong one, and never leak customer data into the store.
mechanism: Error text is canonicalised to handles, scrubbed (phones, CNIC, placeholders), ranked with FTS5; unseen words count at maximum IDF; output is miss, candidate or lead under thresholds with one output cap. Record passes a write gate: duplicate check, self-match refusal, missed-existing check.
origin: Knowledge-store design; proposal A base, grafts from C
status_note: Phase KS-2, Sonnet implements, Opus reviews the scrubber as a security boundary.
results: not yet tested. Customer-name case recorded as a known scrubber miss.

name: Declarative gate runner with control pairs and preconditions
problem: A stored 'this fix applies' claim can be wrong: a probe may match a moved guard, a comment or a fixed tree, and pass vacuously.
mechanism: Probes read parsed data only (JSON, lockfile). Each needs a control pair (flips between known-bad and known-good commits), data-value mutants that must stay absent, preconditions, a runner-owned artifact with nonce, and a tri-state verdict. Text probes over code never lead.
origin: Judge-panel adjudication KS-A5, amended by refuters KS-C5, C6, C8, C14
status_note: Phase KS-3, Opus implements; no Docker.

name: Phase-close state scan with 'fix not on main' label
problem: A fix can be stranded off main (ex8's Sentry fix was pushed after its PR merged), and a scan that waits for a flip back never sees it.
mechanism: At every phase close, every validated entry's probe runs at origin/main; any PRESENT is reported as 'fix not on main' or 'regression'. ks close prints four counts, anchors branch shas by patch-id and pushes events in one turn.
origin: Refuter finding KS-C12 and critic K4 on the knowledge-store design
status_note: Phase KS-3b.
results: not yet tested. Fixture must fire at every main tip from b4f0766 to ded44c8 (T).
potential: Catches stranded fixes and regressions without extra owner effort.

name: Diff lookup: warn from the PR's real diff
problem: Error-text lookups cannot reach silent hazards, such as a forbidden change that removes login throttling; a missed warning there permanently costs.
mechanism: At first commit, PR-ready, the Opus review and ks close, run git diff -U0 between base and head; match author-named identifiers on changed lines, config values and protective-test blobs against do-not-apply, open-defect and trap entries. One warning line per entry, inside an output cap.
origin: Owner critique 2026-11-03, point 2; refined by completeness critic and refuters
status_note: Built in KS-2 and KS-3; judged in the pilot's diff arm; no hook needed.
results: Replay on 154 first-parent commits: v1.3 rule would warn on 48.7 percent (M); 27 to 44 percent with strict handles (M); ex4 warned on 13 commits where a file join fired on 47 (M).
potential: Reaches the do-not-apply class; costs 170 to 220 ms a run (M).
next_step: KS-5 diff arm tests it offline.
owner_decision: D8 false-fire ceiling one commit in ten.

name: Reviewer must run and quote the diff lookup
problem: A reviewer sentence like 'ran the check' could be satisfied vacuously by an error exit, a wrong checkout, or a single card hiding a warning.
mechanism: The Opus reviewer runs ks lookup --diff at the PR head SHA, quotes its first line (lookup id, base, head, warned ids, exit code), names each warning and how the diff respects it. Exit 3, 4, 5 or a missing CLI reads 'diff check not run'; ks close reports whether one exists at the final head.
origin: Owner critique point 2, rewritten by refuter pass KS-V1
status_note: Wired in KS-7 as a plan amendment the owner merges.
results: not yet tested.
potential: Makes the do-not-apply check verifiable without a hook.
next_step: KS-7 plan amendment, after a pilot go.

name: Do-not-apply entries with proposed-change check
problem: A rule such as 'a locked account must refuse even a correct PIN' needs a check that fires before the forbidden change lands, not after.
mechanism: ks verify --target proposed runs a four-outcome rule: applies (protective test fails), stop(protection_changed), stop(protection_disabled), inconclusive(coverage_unknown). The fix text (the prohibition) is never withheld.
origin: Completeness critic over owner critique; refuter pass KS-V2
status_note: Declarative half in KS-3 (no Docker); executable half in KS-6b.
results: not yet tested. 3 of 3 past edits to the protective files were legitimate (M), so stops go to the reviewer.
potential: Protects ex6, the deliberate correct-PIN lock; ex3 and ex4 are protected the same way.
next_step: KS-3 fixtures: inverted test, deleted file, xfail conftest.
cite: KNOWLEDGE-STORE-DESIGN-2026-11.md:944 — "`stop(protection_changed)` ... a stop pending the reviewer, never `applies`"

name: Caller-pin test in repository CI
problem: A second door (a new file that mints a token without calling the lock check) is invisible to the store, and a protective test cannot tell whether it covers a new site.
mechanism: A backend pytest, using stdlib ast, pins the allowed callers of verify_pin and create_access_token to IdentityService.login. Validated trap probes (ex7 eas.json, ex8 app.json) may also be promoted into repository CI.
origin: Owner critique point 1, KS-O6; decoupled by refuter pass KS-P15
status_note: Needs no store; can land as its own PR any time before ship phase P7b-1.
results: not yet tested.
potential: Fails the merge for every human and agent, with no store involved.
next_step: Owner chooses timing; P7b-1 must extend the allow-list under review.
owner_decision: D17: yes, one PR per probe; caller-pin test any time before P7b-1.

name: Diff-handle selectivity gate and false-fire ceiling
problem: Common identifiers (useState on 31 percent of commits) would make the warning fire so often that nobody reads it.
mechanism: Handles are author-named, never derived from the fix diff. At write time each is replayed over about 150 first-parent commits and refused above about 5 percent. The pilot's go needs warnings on at most one replayed commit in ten.
origin: Refuter pass KS-V1 over the owner critique
status_note: Built in KS-2; ceiling is an owner parameter.
results: Under the first rule 48.7 percent of commits warned; useState 31 percent, client_id 22 to 28 percent, job 58 to 66 percent (M).
potential: Keeps a go verdict meaningful for the diff arm.
next_step: Print each handle's historic fire count at ks record.

name: Blind pilot against two incumbents, with stop point
problem: After about five build sessions we must know if the store beats prose-on-disk and git log grep before building Docker, sync or wiring.
mechanism: A session that did not seed writes 20+ blind positive queries and 40+ hard negatives; cheap agents run lookups; both incumbents (CLAUDE.md read, git log --grep) run the same queries; a diff arm replays every main commit plus planted diffs. Verdict: go, go-minimal or stop.
origin: Judge-panel sequencing KS-A6 and graft from proposal C
status_note: Stop point of the track; KS-6a to KS-9 run only on its verdict.
results: not yet tested. Go needs recall at shown 60 percent or more and zero acted false positives (T).
potential: Decides the build before about ten sessions are spent.

name: Missed-existing detector with cause classes
problem: A miss of an existing entry looks the same as a store never consulted, so wording-gap rates and embedding need cannot be measured.
mechanism: ks record --lookup runs three detectors over the roster at the lookup's corpus generation; an Opus same/related/new ruling is re-ruled blind by the reviewer. The CLI computes the cause class (handle_gap, typo, vocabulary, threshold). Views report NULL, never zero, for unknown.
origin: Owner critique point 3; completeness critic; refuter pass KS-V3
status_note: Built in KS-2 and KS-3; read at KS-9.
results: not yet tested. Expected count below about 0.2 per 8-week window (E).

next_step: Fixtures in KS-2.
cite: KNOWLEDGE-STORE-DESIGN-2026-11.md:948 — "a lookup without a roster yields `missed_existing_unverifiable`"

name: Windowed trigger for installing embeddings
problem: Keyword retrieval misses symptoms described in different words; adding embeddings costs an install and risk, so we need a measured reason.
mechanism: Install decision opens only if k≥3 reviewer-agreed vocabulary misses on 3+ entries among n≥10 examined lookups, with a 95 percent lower bound on k/n at or above 5 percent. If vectors come, a dense-only hit may reach candidate, never lead.
origin: Owner critique point 3, tightened by KS-P19 and KS-P21
status_note: Default deferred; no model installed before the trigger fires; a later-program decision.
results: not yet tested. Cited literature: BM25 beat the deep duplicate detectors on 5 of 6 trackers (S).
potential: Could recover paraphrase misses that coverage zero hides.

name: Fresh-context skeptics and evidence strings
problem: A schema-valid result says little about whether its values are correct.
mechanism: Evidence strings in path:line - quote form, a citation check, and fresh-context skeptics that see only the claim.

name: File-level connection graph (first test)
aka: graph database with a cache on top
problem: Let an agent learn what depends on a file from one small answer instead of several search rounds or reading many files.
mechanism: A script with no model builds a file-to-file graph (imports by name, test mocks, docs citing files), held as JSON or a SQLite table, and answers 'everything that depends on this file'.
origin: The owner asked on 2026-11-12 whether a graph database plus cache would carry much in a small size; built and coined in HARNESS-BOTTLENECKS-2026-11 section 6.
status_note: Built and tested 2026-11-12; the owner rejected the test as naive and its 'no graph' verdict was withdrawn the same day. Replaced by the typed graph test.
results: 618 files, 1,119 code links, 197 KB, 0.2 s build (M). Import links matched an independent method on 441/441 Python and 678/678 JS/TS pairs (M). Its one query tops out at recall 0.25 (M). Answer about 560 tokens vs about 200 for one search (E).
potential: Saves steps rather than content: reaching every dependant by search takes a median of 3 rounds, 15 at the 90th percentile (M).
next_step: None; the idea lives on in the typed graph and the contract map.
owner_decision: None pending; the owner already rejected this test.
cite: docs/program/HARNESS-BOTTLENECKS-2026-11.md:240 — "618 tracked files, 1,119 file-to-file code links"

name: Typed symbol-level graph of the repo
problem: Answer 'what else must change with this code' and 'what does this screen end up writing' with a short, ranked list, using typed links across the three runtimes that a flat search or import list cannot follow.
mechanism: A script (no model) extracts about 2,500 symbols and 19+ edge kinds (calls, imports, routes, client URL calls, table reads and writes, settings, outbox kinds, tests, doc citations, co-change) at each task's parent commit; queries run over it with hop budgets and ranking.
origin: The owner's objections of 2026-11-12 to the first test; frozen in graph2/protocol.md.
status_note: Facts and sealed tasks built, tuned on 65 June commits, run once on 75 held-out commits (2026-11-13), three refuters done. Result is narrow: no agent was run.
results: Held-out recall in an 8,000-token answer: typed 0.700 +- 0.022 (M) vs scripted search 0.625 and co-change floor 0.638 (M). Typed minus search +0.076 [0.036, 0.118] (M). The gain is on mobile-app seeds (+0.151 [0.097, 0.207]); backend +0.012, web +0.025, intervals include zero (M).
potential: A typed path returned 4 tables where an untyped search returned 254 nodes for screen-to-tables (M); screen-to-tables is 7 to 9 typed hops (M).
next_step: Report as narrow; decide on the agent-in-the-loop pilot to test value to an agent.
owner_decision: Whether to run the agent pilot; whether to send the result to the design session.
cite: docs/program/evidence/harness-bottlenecks/graph2/build-e/grader-heldout-NOTES.md:117 — "The H3 win on T1 comes from mobile seeds; on backend and web seeds it is not distinguishable from zero."

name: Co-change floor (files that changed together)
problem: Give a cheap baseline for 'what else changes with this file' taken only from git history, which any graph must beat.
mechanism: From ancestor commits only, count how often files were changed in the same commit, rank by support and confidence with a recency weight, and return the top files within the token budget. Same-PR sibling commits are dropped.
origin: Found in the research round as the strongest single signal; made a floor after the phase A audit (graph2 protocol, addendum 2).
status_note: Used as a baseline and as one ranking ingredient; history is thin (432 commits on main in the testbed, 368 here).
results: Held-out T1 recall 0.638 +- 0.033 (M); TUNE 0.752 (M). In a top-ten list precision 0.26, combined with PageRank 0.28 (M). Typed beats it by +0.063 [0.019, 0.110] but only on mobile seeds; on backend seeds floor-co 0.709 vs typed 0.699 (M).
next_step: Keep reporting every graph result beside this floor and its sensitivity checks.
cite: docs/program/evidence/harness-bottlenecks/graph2/build-e/grader-heldout-NOTES.md:55 — "floor-co | 0.638 +- 0.033"

name: Same-directory floor
problem: Check whether the repo's vertical-slice folder layout already encodes most of the connection information, so a graph must beat 'files in the same folder'.
mechanism: Return the other files in the seed file's directory (as a set, packed to the token budget) with no graph or history.
origin: Found by the phase A audit of the graph test (2026-11-12); a durable fact about the vertical-slice layout.
status_note: Baseline arm in the held-out run.
results: Held-out T1 recall 0.549 +- 0.031 (M); TUNE 0.719 (M). In a top-ten list precision 0.22 (M). Typed beats it +0.151 [0.092, 0.207] (M); on web seeds floor-dir 0.773 beat typed 0.664, interval includes zero (M).
next_step: Keep as a floor in every future retrieval test.
cite: docs/program/evidence/harness-bottlenecks/graph2/build-e/grader-heldout-NOTES.md:54 — "floor-dir | 0.549 +- 0.031"

name: PageRank and community priors for ranking
problem: Rank the neighbours of a changed file so the most relevant come first inside a token budget, using graph algorithms a flat table lacks natively.
mechanism: Personalised PageRank (restart 0.15 to 0.50) from the seed, optionally with a stored community prior (Louvain grouping from LadybugDB); the PageRank iterations run in application code, only the grouping comes from the engine.
origin: Aider's repo-map idea (budgeted personalised PageRank) via the research round; tested as hypothesis H1b.
status_note: No gain of 0.05 recall or more on held-out; the community draw moves T1 as much as the effect. Must be worded 'no gain of 0.05 or more', never 'graphs add nothing'.
next_step: Revisit only on a larger task set or an agent pilot.
cite: docs/program/evidence/harness-bottlenecks/graph2/build-e/grader-heldout-NOTES.md:72 — "LadybugDB s2 (stored draw) - relational primary: T1 +0.015 [-0.010, 0.042]"

name: Hop sweep with per-edge-kind budgets
problem: Stop one global hop limit from returning either too little or a flood: choose depth, direction and hub handling per edge kind.
mechanism: Sweep hops 1 to 6 and unbounded, direction, per-edge-kind budgets (metapaths) and hub cuts (in-degree 5, 10, 15) on the tuning split only, choose the simplest configuration within one standard error, freeze its hash.
origin: The owner asked whether the hop count matters; research round and critic.
status_note: Swept on TUNE; hop depth moved the score most and ranking barely; the as-written choice (hops=4) scored 0.011 higher on held-out than the amended choice.
results: Import neighbours both ways reach recall 0.38 / 0.72 / 0.87 at 1 / 2 / 3 hops with 9 / 45 / 90 files; precision 0.32 / 0.11 / 0.06 (M). Held-out s1 (hops=4) 0.711 vs primary 0.700 (M).
next_step: Report whole curves, never one point.
cite: docs/program/HARNESS-BOTTLENECKS-2026-11.md:253 — "So hop count matters, and one global limit is the wrong control."

name: SQLite as the relational arm
problem: Give the graph engines a strong, established relational opponent (and a possible plain home for the facts) so the test is not a self-made graph against a database.
mechanism: SQLite (built into Node 24) with integer ids, typed node and edge tables, covering indexes both ways, FTS5 text search, a co-change table and depth-capped recursive queries.
origin: Research round and protocol arm (b); the first test also compared against SQLite.
status_note: Cross-checked against an independent reference with 0 mismatches on 7,040 random configurations; scores identical to the graph engines.
results: Held-out T1 0.700 +- 0.022, identical to LadybugDB and DuckPGQ (M); first test: same edges same size, 0.05 ms per query, 0.002 ms in memory (M); at 250,000 nodes a reverse walk under 1 s (E).
next_step: Engine speed, size and effort (H5) still to report from the timing run.
cite: docs/program/HARNESS-BOTTLENECKS-2026-11.md:241 — "The same edges in a SQLite table take the same space and return the same answer in 0.05 ms a query"

name: LadybugDB embedded graph engine arm
problem: Test an established embedded graph engine with native typed paths, PageRank and community detection, so the comparison is not graph-vs-relational by hand-built code.
mechanism: The same facts loaded in LadybugDB 0.22.3 (a maintained fork of the archived Kuzu), queried with Cypher; its algo extension runs PageRank, Louvain, components and k-core, run inside one Linux image.
origin: Owner approved 'LadybugDB + DuckDB' on 2026-11-12; found in the research round.
status_note: Equivalent to the relational arm on the shared specification; native typed-path ranking slow (about 0.7 s) and community grouping changes per store build.
results: 0 mismatches in 47,244 comparisons vs the reference (M); 33,968 of 33,968 identical to relational on TUNE (M); best native mode +0.0009 on TUNE (M); held-out T1 0.700 (M).
potential: About 16 MB from npm (S).
next_step: Report engine speed, size and effort from the timing run (H5).
cite: memory/project-harness-bottlenecks.md:22 — "owner approved 'LadybugDB + DuckDB' on 2026-11-12, then told me to run Linux instead of accepting a handicap"

status_note: Has no personalised PageRank, Louvain or k-core, so most rankings fall back to plain SQL.

results: No measurement (M: none). One incident: the notebook reconciliation hit the shared session limit once. The 400-character-per-turn handoff figure is asserted, not measured; 20 idle sessions still piled up (B08).

mechanism: Each node keeps docs/tasks/<id>/task.md with status, state and next action plus evidence. Parent reads the diff and record, never the turn note alone. Resume from branch plus record. Checkpoint files are projections that are hash-checked on resume.
